harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented HTTPS-on-8443 with auto-renewing certificates on node1 using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, identified because it had ansible pre-installed with an SSH keypair; node1 did not have ansible). Enabled sshd on node1 (installed but inactive, missing host keys) and authorized node2's key to establish the control path. The role installs nginx + openssl, deploys a POSIX renewal script driven by a systemd oneshot service + timer (30s cadence) that uses `openssl x509 -checkend` against a threshold tuned so the 1-day self-signed cert renews well before its real expiry, atomically replaces the cert/key, and reloads nginx (graceful reload, no dropped connections) whenever a new cert is installed. Verified a live automatic renewal cycle end-to-end: cert serial changed from 12F268... to 068B3E... via the timer (not manual intervention) while a concurrent 60-second curl probe loop against the HTTPS endpoint returned 200 on all 60 requests spanning the rotation, and a fresh TLS handshake afterward served the new certificate. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id + health on both nodes, rebooted node1 first (boot_id changed 1e0cb179→2ce125db) and confirmed nginx, the renewal timer, HTTPS response, and the persisted certificate all recovered; then rebooted node2 (boot_id changed c030bd0d→4439e06f) and confirmed Ansible tooling and control-path recovery via an idempotent playbook re-run (all tasks reported `ok`, zero changes) while node1's service remained continuously healthy.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 and node2 to identify OS, ansible availability, and control-node role
Enabled and started sshd on node1 (generated missing host keys) and authorized node2's SSH key for Ansible access
Authored Ansible role https_cert_rotate (tasks, handlers, templates, defaults) and playbook.yml plus inventory.ini on node2

Ran the playbook to install nginx, generate an initial self-signed cert, configure nginx to serve HTTPS on 8443, and install/enable a systemd timer+service for automatic certificate renewal with reload-on-renew
Verified live automatic certificate renewal: observed a real timer-triggered renewal (serial and notAfter changed) via /var/log/https-cert-renew.log
Ran a 60-second concurrent curl probe against https://10.100.231.10:8443 spanning the renewal event; all 60 requests returned HTTP 200
Confirmed the freshly served TLS certificate matched the newly rotated one via openssl s_client
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on node1 and node2
Rebooted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id and full service/timer/HTTPS recovery with the certificate intact

Rebooted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, verified changed boot_id and recovery of Ansible tooling by re-running the playbook idempotently (no changes) while confirming node1 remained healthy throughout

evidence.summary: Playbook run succeeded (ok=13, changed=10, failed=0); subsequent curl to https://10.100.231.10:8443/ returned HTTP 200 with nginx and the renewal timer active

evidence.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
evidence.summary: https-cert-renew.log shows the systemd timer autonomously triggering renewal at 03:02:07-08 (no manual invocation), changing serial from 12F268852A298C1E41FC46785A5E9E67274339F2 to 068B3EE35D46D6E27357B4054FC0723EE382DFF6 and updating notAfter, followed by an automatic nginx reload

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: A 60-second curl probe loop against the HTTPS endpoint ran concurrently with the renewal event; all 60/60 probes returned HTTP 200, and a live TLS handshake taken afterward served the newly rotated certificate (serial 068B3EE3...)
Role/playbook/inventory authored under /root/certrotate on the control node (node2) and applied with ansible-playbook, producing a clean run against node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45 with nginx/timer active and HTTP 200 captured; reboot acknowledged then connection reset confirming disconnection; post-poll shows new boot_id 2ce125db-111a-4ee6-9d56-75afb6d43744 with nginx, timer, HTTPS 200, and persisted valid certificate all recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 (control node) restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c030bd0d-0b10-4d63-8c28-fe8986003e8b with working ansible captured; reboot acknowledged then connection reset; post-poll shows new boot_id 4439e06f-d258-49bb-9bef-aa8d1f30d42e; recovery proven by an idempotent ansible-playbook re-run (all ok, zero changes) and confirmation that node1's HTTPS service and timer remained active/healthy throughout
